# 什么是段落嵌入？

- 原标题：What Is Passage Embedding?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/passage-embedding/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

段落嵌入，是一份固定长度的数字列表，用于编码一小段文字——一个句子、一段话或一个检索分块——的含义，使意思相近的段落在共享向量空间中彼此靠近。检索系统比较这些向量，找到与查询最相关的段落，匹配的是含义，而非完全相同的词语。

### 核心要点

- 段落嵌入表示一个文本块，而非整篇文档；同一篇文章会生成多个独立嵌入，每个段落对应一个。
- 含义相关的段落在向量空间中彼此靠近，因此即使查询和文字没有相同关键词，检索仍然能够工作。
- Sentence-BERT（Reimers 与 Gurevych，EMNLP 2019）让这项技术得到推广：在 10,000 个句子中找出最相似的一对，耗时从使用 BERT 时的约 65 小时降到了大约 5 秒。
- 段落嵌入是 AI 答案背后的检索层：系统为你的文本块和用户的问题生成嵌入，再取出距离最近的段落作为候选证据。

### 段落嵌入如何运作

嵌入模型读取一段文字后，会输出固定长度的向量，即一份数字列表，通常包含几百到几千个数字，这就是段落嵌入。模型经过训练，会让含义相近的段落产生指向相近方向的向量，让无关内容产生指向其他方向的向量。含义由此变成几何关系：向量空间中的接近程度，代表语义上的相似程度。

这很重要，因为检索不再依赖共同出现的词语。“如何阻止 AI 机器人抓取我的网站”这样的查询，可以检索到题为“使用 robots.txt 控制爬虫访问”的段落，即使两者几乎没有共同词汇，因为它们的嵌入彼此接近。具体比较通常使用[余弦相似度](https://roborank.io/glossary/cosine-similarity/)，衡量两个向量指向同一方向的程度。

段落嵌入构成了大多数 AI 搜索背后的检索层。系统通过[分块](https://roborank.io/glossary/chunking/)，将网页切分为段落大小的单元，再把每个块的嵌入存入[检索语料库](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-corpus/)。回答问题时，系统为用户的问题生成嵌入，并执行[分块检索](https://roborank.io/glossary/chunk-retrieval/)，取出嵌入最接近的段落。这些段落成为[检索增强生成](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation/)系统综合生成答案的候选证据。模型最容易直接提取的段落，则成为[事实依据来源](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding-source/)。

### 段落嵌入与文档嵌入

最容易让人混淆的区别是粒度。文档嵌入把整页压缩为一个向量，将所有内容混合在一起：一篇涉及十个子主题、长达 2,000 词的文章被压成一个点，因此针对第七个子主题的查询，检索到的是整篇稀释后的平均值。段落嵌入让各个块保持独立，因此能够单独检索到真正回答问题的那一段，其含义不被稀释。这就是检索系统绝大多数采用段落级嵌入的原因，也是内容如何分块会直接影响哪些信息能被找到的原因。

### 段落嵌入示例

实用段落嵌入最清楚、最有文献依据的起点，是 Nils Reimers 和 Iryna Gurevych 在 **EMNLP 2019** 论文中提出的 **Sentence-BERT（SBERT）**。在 SBERT 之前，用 BERT 比较句子，意味着每次比较都要把两个句子一起输入网络。论文报告，在 **10,000 个句子的集合中找出最相似的一对，需要约 5,000 万次推理计算，耗时约 65 小时**。这使得在真实语料库上进行语义搜索难以落地。

SBERT 的解决方法，是使用孪生网络独立地将每个段落嵌入为固定向量，因此整个集合只需计算一次嵌入。此后，比较段落就只是比较向量。论文最醒目的数字体现了收益：同样的最相似句对搜索，**从约 65 小时降到了约 5 秒**——计算 10,000 个嵌入约需 5 秒，再花约 **0.01 秒**使用余弦相似度进行比较，同时保持 BERT 级别的准确度。向量只需预先计算一次，此后的每次查询成本都很低。

现代检索正是采用这样的架构。OpenAI 的 text-embedding-3 系列等托管模型，通过一次 API 调用就能把任意一段文字转换为向量；向量数据库则存储数百万个段落嵌入，支持快速最近邻查找。SBERT 证明的原则贯穿整个 AI 搜索：每个段落只嵌入一次，然后让低成本的向量比较完成检索。这也解释了面向 AI 可见性写作时的一条实用原则：既然检索发生在段落层面，文本块才是你真正优化的对象。自成一体的段落会嵌入成一个明确、可被找到的点；散落在多个段落中的观点，则会嵌入成更模糊的点，与本应找到它的查询距离更远。

### 人们常犯的错误

我看到团队常犯的错误，是只优化页面，却忘了真正被嵌入和检索的单位是段落。AI 系统并不存储“你的整篇文章”；它把文章切成文本块，再为每一块存储独立向量。如果你想让人引用的事实散落在三个段落里，就没有一个段落嵌入能清晰捕捉全部含义，最终检索到的文本块只包含一半的陈述。我见过页面失去引用，并非因为信息不存在，而是因为信息分散在整个章节里，没有在一个独立段落中完整说明。写作时，要让每个观点都完整存在于一个文本块中，无论放在原位置阅读，还是单独提取出来，含义都保持一致——因为在向量索引中，它确实会被单独提取。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是段落嵌入？

它是一个固定长度的数字向量，用来表示一句话或一段话等短文本的含义。系统比较这些向量，找到含义与查询匹配的段落，实现不依赖共同关键词的语义检索。

#### 段落嵌入与文档嵌入有何不同？

段落嵌入表示一个文本块——句子、段落或检索单元；文档嵌入则尝试用一个向量概括整个页面。段落级嵌入的检索更精确，因为某个具体观点不会被文档其余内容稀释。

#### AI 搜索如何使用段落嵌入？

系统将页面切成文本块，为每一块生成嵌入并存储向量。用户提问时，它也为问题生成嵌入，再检索嵌入距离最近的段落。这些检索出的段落成为生成答案时的候选证据。

#### 哪种模型生成段落嵌入？

文本嵌入模型。Sentence-BERT 于 2019 年提出高效的句子级嵌入，而 OpenAI 的 text-embedding-3 系列等现代托管模型，可以通过一次 API 调用生成段落嵌入。它们都会把一段文字转换成包含数百或数千个数字的向量。

### 结论

段落嵌入将一块文字转换为语义空间中的坐标，在那里，距离代表相似程度。正因如此，AI 搜索才能把问题匹配到一个从未重复问题用词的段落；也正因如此，真正的优化单元是段落，而不是页面。让每个文本块清楚地表达一件事，它的嵌入才会落在相关查询能够找到的位置上。

## 英文原文

A passage embedding is a fixed-length list of numbers that encodes the meaning of a short span of text — a sentence, paragraph, or retrieval chunk — so that passages with similar meaning land close together in a shared vector space. Retrieval systems compare these vectors to find the passages most relevant to a query, matching on meaning rather than exact words.

### Key Takeaways

- A passage embedding represents a chunk of text, not a whole document — the same article produces many separate embeddings, one per passage.
- Passages with related meaning end up near each other in vector space, so retrieval works even when the query and the text share no keywords.
- The technique was popularized by Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych, EMNLP 2019), which cut finding the most similar pair among 10,000 sentences from about 65 hours with BERT to roughly 5 seconds.
- Passage embeddings are the retrieval layer beneath AI answers: a system embeds your chunks, embeds the user’s question, and pulls the closest passages as candidate evidence.

### How Passage Embedding Works

A passage embedding is produced by an embedding model that reads a span of text and outputs a fixed-length vector — a list of numbers, often several hundred to a few thousand of them. The model is trained so that passages meaning similar things produce vectors pointing in similar directions, and passages about unrelated things produce vectors pointing elsewhere. Meaning becomes geometry: closeness in the vector space stands in for similarity in meaning.

This matters because retrieval no longer depends on shared words. A query like “how do I stop AI bots from scraping my site” can retrieve a passage titled “controlling crawler access with robots.txt” even though the two share almost no vocabulary, because their embeddings land near each other. The comparison itself is usually done with [cosine similarity](https://roborank.io/glossary/cosine-similarity/), which scores how closely two vectors point in the same direction.

Passage embeddings are the retrieval layer beneath most AI search. A system takes your pages, splits them through [chunking](https://roborank.io/glossary/chunking/) into passage-sized units, and stores one embedding per chunk in a [retrieval corpus](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-corpus/). At answer time it embeds the user’s question and runs [chunk retrieval](https://roborank.io/glossary/chunk-retrieval/) to pull the passages whose embeddings sit closest. Those passages become the candidate evidence a [retrieval-augmented generation](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation/) system synthesizes into an answer. The passage the model can most cleanly lift becomes the [grounding source](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding-source/).

### Passage Embedding vs Document Embedding

The distinction that trips people up is granularity. A document embedding compresses an entire page into a single vector, which blurs everything together — a 2,000-word article about ten subtopics collapses into one point, so a query about subtopic seven retrieves the whole diluted average. A passage embedding keeps each chunk separate, so the specific paragraph that answers the query can be retrieved on its own, at full strength. This is why retrieval systems overwhelmingly embed at the passage level, and why how you chunk your content directly shapes what can be found.

### Example of Passage Embedding

The clearest documented origin of practical passage embeddings is **Sentence-BERT (SBERT)**, introduced by Nils Reimers and Iryna Gurevych in a paper published at **EMNLP 2019**. Before SBERT, comparing sentences with BERT meant feeding both sentences through the network together for every comparison — the paper reports that finding the most similar pair in a collection of **10,000 sentences required roughly 50 million inference computations, about 65 hours**. That made semantic search over a real corpus impractical.

SBERT’s fix was to embed each passage independently into a fixed vector using a siamese network, so a collection only needs to be embedded once. After that, comparing passages is just comparing vectors. The paper’s headline number is the payoff: the same most-similar-pair search **drops from about 65 hours to roughly 5 seconds** — the 5 seconds to compute the 10,000 embeddings, plus about **0.01 seconds** to compare them with cosine similarity — while preserving BERT-level accuracy. The vectors are precomputed once; every query afterward is cheap.

That architecture is exactly how modern retrieval works. Hosted models such as OpenAI’s text-embedding-3 family turn any span of text into a vector through a single API call, and vector databases store millions of those passage embeddings for fast nearest-neighbor lookup. The principle SBERT proved holds throughout AI search: embed each passage once, then let cheap vector comparison do the retrieval. It also explains a practical rule for anyone writing for AI visibility — since retrieval happens at the passage level, the chunk is what you are really optimizing. A self-contained passage embeds to a distinct, findable point; a claim smeared across several paragraphs embeds to a vaguer one that sits further from the queries meant to find it.

### The thing people get wrong

The mistake I see teams make is optimizing the page and forgetting the passage is the unit that actually gets embedded and retrieved. An AI system does not store "your article" — it slices the article into chunks and stores a separate vector for each one. If a fact you want cited is spread across three paragraphs, no single passage embedding captures it cleanly, and the chunk that gets retrieved carries only half the claim. I have seen pages lose citations not because the information was missing but because it was smeared across a section instead of stated inside one self-contained passage. Write so that each idea lives in a chunk that means the same thing whether it is read in place or lifted out alone — because in a vector index, it will be lifted out alone.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is a passage embedding?

It is a fixed-length numeric vector that represents the meaning of a short span of text, such as a sentence or paragraph. Systems compare these vectors to find passages whose meaning matches a query, enabling semantic retrieval that does not depend on shared keywords.

#### How is a passage embedding different from a document embedding?

A passage embedding represents one chunk — a sentence, paragraph, or retrieval unit — while a document embedding tries to summarize a whole page in one vector. Passage-level embeddings retrieve more precisely because a specific claim is not diluted by the rest of the document.

#### How are passage embeddings used in AI search?

The system splits pages into chunks, embeds each chunk, and stores the vectors. When a user asks a question, it embeds the question too, then retrieves the passages whose embeddings are closest. Those retrieved passages become the candidate evidence for the generated answer.

#### What model creates passage embeddings?

Text embedding models do. Sentence-BERT introduced efficient sentence-level embeddings in 2019, and modern hosted models like OpenAI’s text-embedding-3 family produce passage embeddings through an API call. Each turns a span of text into a vector of hundreds or thousands of numbers.

### The Bottom Line

A passage embedding turns a chunk of writing into coordinates in meaning-space, where distance stands in for similarity. It is the reason AI search can match a question to a paragraph that never repeats the question’s words — and the reason the passage, not the page, is the real unit of optimization. Make each chunk mean one thing cleanly, and its embedding lands where the right queries can find it.
